answer.rationale: Competitor has triggered immediate price-based churn in the SMB segment. Memory 73 confirms promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB acquisition and revenue lift. A standard experiment on promotional pricing targets the acute threat directly while limiting downside risk—this is time-critical competitive defense, not growth optimization. The retention risk is real: we've seen -1% dips before (exp_31). However, doing nothing cedes market share and allows churn to accelerate. A bounded, measured promotional response on SMB preserves optionality: we can layer in onboarding simplification (memory_86, memory_31) and activation messaging (memory_91) after the promotional stabilization if needed. Enterprise sales assistance (memory_44) does not address price sensitivity and has longer sales cycles incompatible with week-level churn urgency. Referral incentives (memory_57) work on established customers but don't address new acquisition or existing account churn. This decision assumes promotional pricing will be time-limited and paired with value communication to preserve unit economics. Confidence is moderate because we're extrapolating from day-31 memory under different competitive conditions, but the threat is immediate and memory_73 is the only directly relevant signal we possess.
